mappings.applicability_reason: Export generation consumes significant compute in the Export Worker and object storage capacity in the managed object store, and this work is triggered by customer-initiated requests over the public Export API rather than by the system itself, so repeated external triggers can drive resource consumption, matching the requirement’s conditions on externally triggered, resource-consuming processing.
assumptions: Assume that assembling exports and writing them to the managed object store is non-trivial work whose repeated triggering can materially affect worker capacity and storage usage, as reflected in the documented architecture and operations context.

mappings.applicability_reason: The system retains export files as working data in a managed object store after processing completes, and documentation describes both immediate deletion after customer download and a 30-day storage lifecycle policy, so the requirement about defining and enforcing retention for sensitive working data applies to these exports and their impact on storage usage in this threat.
assumptions: It is unknown which document, if either, reflects the customer-facing description of export file retention, so alignment with what customers are told cannot be determined from the available material.

documentation_gaps.title: Bounding of export-triggered work is not documented
documentation_gaps.description: The documentation for the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store does not describe any rate limits, per-customer or global quotas, queue-depth limits, or other bounds on how many exports can be requested or processed over a period. Because export generation is non-trivial work that writes export files to storage, and exports are triggered by customer requests over a public API, this absence means it is not possible to determine from the documentation whether repeated or malicious export requests can drive unbounded consumption of worker capacity or storage, as in threat thr-006.
documentation_gaps.importance: Without documented bounds on export frequency, size, or concurrent jobs, it is unclear whether the system can protect itself against a customer or attacker repeatedly triggering exports and exhausting worker or storage resources, which is central to assessing the denial-of-service risk described in thr-006.
requested_evidence: Documentation describing any per-customer, per-account, or global rate limits or quotas applied to Export API requests and export jobs.
Documentation of any queue depth limits, backpressure mechanisms, or other controls that bound the number of in-flight export jobs.
Documentation of any cost, storage, or time-based ceilings that constrain export processing triggered by external customer requests.

documentation_gaps.title: Export file retention behaviour is inconsistently documented
documentation_gaps.description: Architecture documentation describes export files in the managed object store as temporary working data that are deleted immediately once the customer has downloaded them (evd-003), while operations documentation states that a storage lifecycle policy retains completed export files for 30 days before expiring them (evd-006). This contradiction means the actual retention period and behaviour for export files, and whether it is consistently represented in product-facing documentation, cannot be determined from the available material.
documentation_gaps.importance: The length of time export files are retained affects both resource consumption relevant to threat thr-006 and whether retention of sensitive working data matches what customers are told, which is the focus of req-DATA-002. Without resolving the inconsistency between immediate deletion and 30-day retention, it is not possible to verify that the retention period is clearly defined, enforced, and accurately documented.
requested_evidence: A canonical description of the intended and actual retention behaviour for export files in the managed object store, including when they are deleted after successful download and any lifecycle policies applied.
Customer-facing documentation or policy that states how long export files are retained, so alignment between implementation and customer expectations can be evaluated.
Clarification of which document (architecture overview vs operations guide) is authoritative for describing export file retention, and updates if one is outdated.
